_about: Record contracts: what each job type's record folder must hold. Shipped defaults, read by runtime/records-check.py (docs/PROJECT-TEAM.md, "Records against the process").
marks: file names (globs, top level of the folder) that say a record folder is this job's record. A folder may mark more than one job.

owner: who acts on this job's flags. close: true when the job closes through predict-gate.sh close (a work-order-closed event in the ops ledger); false when it does not; null when the job says nothing about closing.

require: each artefact the folder must hold. check is one of: prediction (each moves.prediction<R>.json parses under predict-gate's own checker and names a move), baseline / measured (each prediction round's file exists and is flat JSON), nonempty (a file matching glob exists and is not empty), mutations (the file matching glob is a reviewer's mutation record: a JSON list of {id, mutation, site, gate, verdict, disposition}; docs/PROJECT-TEAM.md, "The reviewer's mutation record"). An empty file always fails.

per: the artefact is owed once for each file matching this glob, named by putting what the per glob's * matched into the artefact glob's *: findings.md owes mutations.json, findings-fix1.md owes mutations-fix1.json. A re-check in the same folder writes its own file. A file matching the glob that no per file owes is not read.
nested: true reads this job's records at any depth inside a work order's record folder, not only at its top level: a reviewer writes in a subfolder of the step folder it reviews.
active: false lists an artefact whose format is not defined yet. It is reported, never flagged. Switch it on here, in this file, when its format is defined.

Step folders: a folder whose name matches the binding's reviewName ({n} any step number, case ignored) is a step record. A work order is a refactor when one of its folders marks the job with close false and holds no prediction. In a refactor, a step folder that holds no prediction is that job's record (it owes its proof). A refactor never closes: a step without its proof, or a code commit that comes after the latest step proof, is flagged refactor.byte-identical. Outside a refactor, a step folder, or a folder holding a file in marksOutsideRefactor, is a record of the job with close true.

rounds: a review round's file names, declared once. first: the first review's findings and mutations files. fix: the re-check of fix round N ({n} = N, 1 or more), in the same review folder. log: the mutation runner's append-only batch log beside that round's mutations file, one JSON line per verdict, written before the row; records-check reconciles every row that carries a batch id with it. like: the words (case ignored) that make a .md file findings-like; a findings-like file that is not a declared name, and that no other job's marks claim, is refused by the stop check and flagged by records-check (rule reviewer.rounds). from: a file added before this date is history and is never flagged. The brief templates and the reviewer's prompt state these names literally; runtime/tests keeps them equal.
testRoots: the folders a reviewer's `test-added <path>` may name without a test name (`path::name` names one in any file). A binding's 'records.testRoots' replaces them.

A binding may ADD artefacts to a job through its 'records' field, never remove or replace one. promoteAt: a rule flagged on this many work orders or more is a promote-to-code candidate for the owner. windowDays: the window when the binding sets no 'records.since'.
